useCases.sensing: high-res and zoom camera, crack detection
useCases.reason: Undersides and piers need access gear and DIN 1076 needs a qualified engineer; drones capture images, a legged robot only covers deck and embankment.

useCases.sensing: thermal and visual camera, gas and water detection
useCases.reason: Fixed long route with light sensing; quadruped pilots already run in cable tunnels, ladders in shafts stay a limit.

useCases.sensing: camera, crack and coating damage detection, position logging
useCases.reason: Walk paved decks and ramps and photograph defects with position; documentation only, the engineer judges.

useCases.sensing: thermal and zoom camera, analogue gauge reading
useCases.reason: Legged robots with thermal and zoom cameras already patrol switchyards on gravel.

useCases.sensing: bar positions from the structural plan
useCases.reason: Load-bearing reinforcement at engineer-set positions on an open print site; structural work stays with people.
The batching plant is already automated; the operator job is process judgement where a stop ruins the print.

useCases.sensing: planned box and opening positions, print layer height
useCases.reason: Parts are light, but the robot must work beside a running printer on site ground up to 3 m high and in step with the print.

useCases.sensing: carton detection in a dense stack
useCases.reason: Cartons up to 25 kg stacked to the roof exceed most humanoid payloads; dedicated truck-unloading robots exist in parcel logistics.
Euro pallets up to 1.5 t move by pallet truck or autonomous forklift, not by an arm robot.

useCases.sensing: part recognition, barcode and label reading
useCases.reason: Light small parts picked from shelving against a list; the variable mix suits a mobile picker with integration work.
Spraying is feasible, but vibrators up to 39.5 kg and 73 kg trowels must be lifted into a wet, cement-laden wash bay.

useCases.tool: appliance tester, test leads and adapters
useCases.sensing: visual cable and housing damage check
useCases.reason: Plugging leads and running the tester is feasible, but DGUV V3 needs a qualified person and a missed defect is critical.
Parts up to 18.8 kg and 2 m long come off a mixed truck load, near the payload limit of current humanoids.

useCases.tool: drill and screwdriver for fixings, sealing tools
useCases.reason: Windows of 40 to 80 kg must be lifted, aligned and sealed; heavy precise handling needs a lifter or a dedicated cell.
Panels of 49 to 94 kg must be held to an 8 mm joint and riveted for wind suction, far above general-purpose payloads.
Light tape, but clean folding into the corners of varying openings is fine finger work at research level.
Outdoor work from a gondola at height; dedicated arms on the building maintenance unit are offered for exactly this.
Autonomous scrubber-dryers already do this; a humanoid would only drive a machine that drives itself.

useCases.sensing: cameras, thermal imaging, door and water detection
useCases.reason: Walking a fixed route through corridors and stairwells and reporting exceptions; security robots and robot dogs already do it.

useCases.sensing: thermal camera, gauge reading, acoustic monitoring
useCases.reason: Fixed inspection route over floors and stairs with sensing only; robot dogs run such rounds today.
Light parts, but small screws and changing sash sizes need fine work; hardware fitting machines already cover part of it.

useCases.sensing: pane square and on its blocks
useCases.reason: Fragile panes of 20 to 60 kg go on vacuum lifters or automated glazing lines.
Glazed windows of 30 to 90 kg are far above general-purpose payloads and need lifters.
Lifting 30 kg bags all day is above sustained humanoid payload; mixed-case palletising robots do it better.

useCases.sensing: barcode or RFID scanning, vision counting
useCases.reason: Walk to shelf locations and count or scan without moving items; a mobile robot with a scanner can do this.
Tote moves under 15 kg are where the first commercial humanoid deployment runs.
Pallets and board packs of hundreds of kilograms go by forklift or truck crane outdoors.
6 m bars of 22 to 32 kg are long and heavy; bar feeders and saws with magazines fit better.
Light spools labelled and placed in floor racks; the challenge is recognition, which suits a mobile picker.

useCases.tool: pipe cutter, deburrer, battery press machine
useCases.reason: Light pipes, but positioning the press jaw and checking insertion marks is fine tool work at research level.
Boards of 21 to 32 kg held against walls and overhead on ceilings while screwing are at the edge of humanoid payloads; only research prototypes with lighter boards exist.

useCases.sensing: box and cable route positions from the plan
useCases.reason: Light parts, but fine cable routing and box fixing in a tight module is research-level dexterity.
Modules of up to 12 t move by crane or gantry.
Measuring a demoulded element against its drawing is sensing work a mobile robot with a scanner can do.
Parts are light, but placement must match each drawing across a wide pallet; shuttering robots already set some magnets.

useCases.sensing: bar positions from the reinforcement drawing
useCases.reason: Mesh up to 132 kg in structurally set positions; plant systems place reinforcement from CAD.
Shuttering and deshuttering robots already do exactly this.
Members of 50 to 800 kg and several metres long move by crane and conveyor.
Heavy, floppy 40 to 60 kg boards are handled by panel placement robots on modern lines.
CNC joinery centres already cut and joint members far above any robot payload.
Light items at changing locations with tolerant errors; fits a mobile robot well.
Large insulation panels and render over square metres go to gantries or spray robots.
A butterfly turning table flips multi-tonne elements.

useCases.sensing: part recognition, bin and label reading
useCases.reason: Light fittings picked from bins against a part list; high variety favours a mobile picker over a fixed cell.
Batts are light but floppy and bulky; grasping compliant material is unsolved and gluing-insulation cells exist.
Light totes and tool boxes carried on people-sized walkways; a mobile robot can fetch them.
Small parts at a fixed clean-zone station; a humanoid can do it, though a fixed cobot is cheaper once the mix is stable.
Full-format boards above payload limits; gluing and sheathing cells already exist.
A multifunction nailing bridge drives thousands of structural fasteners per shift.
Light repeated pick and place a robot can do, though a fixed pick-and-place cell is cheaper at stable volumes.
Light cartons in a fixed pattern are a classic cobot task; a humanoid could do it but adds cost.
A panel processing centre handles 40 to 60 kg boards in the dust zone.

useCases.sensing: camera, label reading, fitting completeness check
useCases.reason: Zero payload and pure perception; a mobile robot with cameras can photograph and log elements.
Stud insertion robots already place studs of up to 25 kg in structural joints.
Whole elements of several tonnes go by crane and forklift.
Multi-tonne elements move by overhead crane, turning table and transfer carriage.
